name: Zhoushan
title: Zhoushan Ship Repair UTM | Drydock Thickness Measurement
description: Thickness measurement in Zhoushan shipyards: renewal survey and ESP gauging, pre-docking steel estimates and CAP work on tankers and bulk carriers in dock.
h1: Thickness Measurement at the Zhoushan Ship-Repair Yards
intro: The Zhoushan archipelago, off the Zhejiang coast, is one of the busiest ship-repair centres in the world, with docks able to take VLCCs, large ore carriers and big container ships. Superintendents book dockings here for renewal surveys, steel renewal and retrofit work, and need gauging that keeps pace with the yard programme. Our technicians come from India for the length of the dock period and work alongside the class surveyor and the yard's steel department until the survey items are closed.
keywords: combined cap and renewal survey gauging

highlights.p: A Zhoushan dock period is planned around steel. Readings issued space by space, with substantial and excessive wastage flagged the same day, let the yard order and cut plate while tanks are still open and staged.
Gauging on a preceding voyage, at a discharge port or at the Zhoushan anchorages gives the yard a steel renewal estimate before the ship enters dock, so the specification reflects measured condition.

Many scrubbers and ballast water treatment systems were installed in these yards. Their wash-water, overboard and sea-water piping and shell penetrations are now reaching the age where gauging and crack detection matter.

port.h: Zhoushan: an island ship-repair cluster for the largest ships
p: Zhoushan is an archipelago of many islands at the mouth of Hangzhou Bay, joined to Ningbo on the mainland by a chain of road bridges. Its repair yards are spread across several of the islands, and between them they offer graving docks and floating docks sized for the largest tankers, ore carriers and container ships trading to China. COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry runs one of the major repair yards here and has been adding dock capacity, and a number of private repair yards work alongside the state-owned groups, which gives owners a wider choice of dock dates than a single-yard port can offer.

Ships come to Zhoushan for the work that needs a dock: renewal (special) surveys with their close-up survey and gauging, intermediate docking surveys, hull blasting and coating, propeller and rudder work, and steel renewal. The yards were also among the main retrofit centres when scrubbers and ballast water treatment systems were fitted across the global fleet, and much of that equipment, with its piping and shell penetrations, is now coming round for its own inspection and repair. Tankers and bulk carriers at their third or later renewal survey bring the heaviest gauging scope — extensive measurement of cargo and ballast tank structure under the enhanced survey programme.

What makes gauging distinctive here is pace. A large repair yard runs many ships at once, and a ship's dock period is planned around steel: the sooner the extent of renewal is known, the sooner plates can be ordered, cut and fitted. Gauging that arrives late, or in a form the class surveyor cannot use, holds up the whole programme. The useful work starts before the ship arrives, with pre-docking gauging and a clear measurement plan, and continues in dock with the readings delivered space by space as tanks are cleaned, ventilated and staged.

facilities.h: Gauging inside the Zhoushan repair yards
p: Hull gauging in Zhoushan happens almost entirely inside a yard, either in dock or at the yard's repair quays. In dock, the team gauges bottom and side shell, cargo and ballast tanks, and holds as they are made available; at the quay, work continues on deck structure, piping and tanks once the ship has floated out. The yard controls access, hot work and staging, so every day starts with the yard's own permit and safety routine, and the gauging sequence follows the yard's cleaning and staging plan rather than our own preference.

Coordination between three parties decides how well a docking goes: the owner's superintendent, who sets the scope; the class surveyor, who decides where readings are needed and verifies them; and the yard, which renews the steel. We issue readings on the class TM report formats with substantial and excessive wastage marked, so the yard can raise steel renewal quantities and the surveyor can confirm the extent before plates are cut. The gauging programme is shared with whoever runs the blasting and coating schedule as well, because blasting, coating and gauging compete for the same tank access and staging, and their order has to be agreed tank by tank.
list: COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry (Zhoushan) — renewal survey gauging, steel renewal estimates and re-gauging of renewed areas on large tankers, bulk carriers and container ships in dock.
Private repair yards across the archipelago — docking-survey gauging and piping inspection for owners booking mid-sized tankers, bulk carriers and container ships.
Repair quays and lay-by berths — completion of deck, piping and tank gauging after undocking while the ship finishes its yard programme afloat.
Scrubber and ballast water treatment installations — wash-water, overboard and sea-water piping gauging, with crack detection at shell penetrations and pipe supports.
Zhoushan anchorages — pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks and holds while the ship waits for its dock to become free.

context.h: Survey, emission and market context for Zhoushan dockings
p: Ships docking in Zhoushan sit under the Tokyo MoU port state control regime while in Chinese waters, but the stronger regulatory driver here is class. The yard period is where the renewal survey requirements of IACS UR Z7, and for ESP ships the requirements of UR Z10.1 to Z10.5 and the 2011 ESP Code, have to be met. For oil tankers, chemical tankers and bulk carriers at the third renewal survey and beyond, the gauging covers transverse sections, cargo and ballast tank structure and suspect areas, and it must be complete and reviewed before the surveyor can close the survey.

Commercially, Zhoushan competes on dock capacity for the largest ships, and international owners send tankers and bulk carriers here alongside the Chinese fleets. Charterers' vetting and oil-major requirements push older tankers toward CAP, which needs a thorough gauging record, and an owner can plan a CAP survey and a renewal survey into the same dock period. Scrubber-fitted ships also bring China's domestic emission rules into the yard discussion: open-loop discharge is restricted in some Chinese waters, and repairs to wash-water systems are often scheduled into the docking.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Zhoushan yards
jobs.p: Zhoushan work runs to the yard's timetable. The scope is agreed with the superintendent and checked against the class requirements before mobilisation; the team arrives for the docking date, works through the spaces as the yard opens them, and stays until the class surveyor has the readings needed to close the survey items. Planning starts well ahead because the team needs Chinese visas.
list: Third renewal survey gauging on a VLCC in dock, covering transverse sections, cargo and ballast tank structure and suspect areas, with substantial corrosion flagged daily to the yard.
Combined CAP and renewal survey gauging on an ageing Suezmax, planned so the CAP measurement record and the class TM report come from one consistent set of readings.
Pre-docking gauging of a Capesize bulk carrier's holds and ballast tanks at anchorage while it waits for its dock, giving the yard an early steel renewal estimate.
Re-gauging of renewed and doubled areas after steel work, so the final TM report reflects the as-repaired condition before the ship undocks.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging, with magnetic particle crack detection at shell penetrations and pipe supports, on a container ship docked for its intermediate survey.

logistics: Access to the archipelago is through Ningbo Lishe International Airport or Shanghai Pudong, then by road over the bridges that link the islands to the mainland; Zhoushan Putuoshan Airport handles domestic flights. Yard access is controlled by the yard itself, with gate passes, safety induction and work permits arranged through the owner's site team or the ship's agent. Technicians travel from India on Chinese business visas, and the invitation letter the visa application needs is easiest to obtain once the docking contract is signed — so tell us the dock date as soon as it is fixed.

faqs.q: Is there value in measuring before the ship arrives at the Zhoushan yard?
faqs.a: Yes, and it helps the dock programme. Pre-docking gauging during a previous port call, or while the ship waits at anchorage, gives the yard an estimate of steel renewal before the ship docks, so plate can be ordered and the work planned. The readings are then confirmed or extended in dock, alongside the class surveyor's close-up survey.

faqs.q: How do you work with the yard and the class surveyor during the docking?
faqs.a: The superintendent sets the scope, the class surveyor indicates the areas and sections to be measured, and the yard provides cleaning, ventilation, lighting and staging. We gauge in the sequence the yard opens spaces, issue readings daily with substantial and excessive wastage marked, and attend the surveyor's review so questions about locations or values are resolved on the spot.

faqs.q: Is it worth combining CAP gauging with the renewal survey in Zhoushan?
faqs.a: For a tanker heading toward its fourth renewal survey, or one charterers are already asking about, it usually is. The tank access, cleaning and staging needed for renewal survey gauging are the same conditions CAP measurement needs. Planning both scopes together avoids opening, cleaning and staging the same tanks twice, and gives the owner one consistent set of readings.

faqs.q: What happens if gauging finds more wastage than the yard planned for?
faqs.a: We flag it as soon as the readings are taken, not at the end of the docking. The superintendent and yard can then decide on additional renewal while the tank is still open and staged, and the class surveyor sees the extent of the problem directly. Late surprises are what extend dock periods; early, complete readings let the owner make the decision with time to act.
